headline: UNIDIR examined whether nuclear deterrence is possible amid the Iran talks and marked Disarmament Week with pieces on cyber crises and international law, as ChinaTalk made the case for cutting China off from DUV lithography equipment.

points.text: UNIDIR examined whether nuclear deterrence is possible in the context of the Iran talks.
SIPRI assessed the state of play for women in multilateral peace operations in 2026.
UNIDIR argued the future of international law in cyberspace needs more diverse voices, as the rules governing state conduct extend into the digital sphere.
UNIDIR marked Disarmament Week with a piece on preparing for cyber crises before they occur, warning that cybersecurity is not merely a technical challenge when critical infrastructure is affected.
ChinaTalk made the case for cutting China off from deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography equipment.
A US Air Force F-22 pilot served as an airborne 'quarterback,' controlling an Anduril-made unmanned FQ-44 Collaborative Combat Aircraft in flight.
Leading AI companies are quietly building a national self-governing structure to oversee their technology, as the federal government stays largely hands-off.
Security teams are confronting AI models that suddenly refuse to help investigate cyberattacks, a growing problem as AI giants race to fend off AI-enabled cyber threats.
